title: A number that springs back says why it did
goal: Type a width a layer will not take and the box comes back to the width it kept, with nothing to say why. Anyone watching sees a box that ignored them rather than a layer that refused. The line under Position & Size should carry the reason for a few seconds, the way it already does when you click a number you cannot type.
notes:
Decided in docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md section 4, "What a control shows after a set the picked things refused": nothing moved at all -> the control returns to the value it had AND the line under the section carries the reason, in the wording law two halves, with no toast. The read-back half landed on 2026-09-06 (GeometryNumberField now sets then re-reads geometrySelection); this is the half that was left.

GeometryInspector.swift already has the mechanism: `explaining: LayerGeometryField?` puts a sentence in the caption line for 6 seconds, but it only answers for READ-ONLY fields via LayerGeometrySelection.explanation(for:). A refusal on a typeable field needs its own state and its own sentence. The reason itself is not in LayerGeometrySelection today: LayerGeometryEditing.minimumWidth only knows the text floor, while a group refused by its own flow (GroupLayout.minWidth/maxWidth, the Layout section Smallest and Largest rows) is refused inside Layer.resized(to:). Either plumb the group layout limits into LayerGeometryEditing so note(for:) warns before you type as well, or work the sentence out from the before/after pair the commit already has.

Scripts/playtest/width-reads-back-walk.json is the walk that sets a Smallest width of 160 on a Button and types 50.

Triage 2026-09-07, design review: the line under a section is now doing three jobs with no shared rule, so settle the rule here rather than adding a fourth use of it later. The three: the standing caption ('Up or down arrow steps by 1, Shift by 10'), the six second explanation of why a number cannot be typed, and the refusal reason this task adds. Evidence: audit 2026-09-06-a-decided-number-looks-decided rough 4 says the standing caption still promises stepping on three fields that are now plain text, and the same audit records a stale-explanation bug where the six second message outlived the rule it was explaining.
acceptance: Typing a width the picked layers refuse puts a plain sentence in the line under Position & Size
The sentence names the rule that refused it, not the field
The line goes back to its usual caption on its own, and at once if a different layer is picked
Nothing at all is said when the layers take the number as typed
One rule is written down for that line and every use of it follows: what it may say, which message wins when two want it at once, and how long each stays
The standing caption under Position & Size stops describing controls that are not there, so a section whose numbers are mostly plain text does not still promise arrow key stepping
Verified in the probe with a real screen capture

log.note: Triage 2026-09-07: folded in the design review finding that the line under a panel section is doing three jobs with no shared rule. Two acceptance items added.
